name: Harp
group: Things people make > Toys > Make music with it > Pluck or strum strings

features.claim: A harp is usually shaped like a triangle.
features.quote: Most commonly, harps are made of wood and are triangular in shape.

features.claim: A harp is mostly made of wood.
features.quote: Most commonly, harps are made of wood and are triangular in shape.

features.claim: A harp has strings that run at a slant to its soundboard.
features.quote: The harp is a stringed musical instrument that has individual strings running at an angle to its soundboard; the strings are plucked with the fingers.

features.claim: A harp has a neck, a resonator and strings.
features.quote: All harps have a neck, resonator, and strings, frame harps or triangular harps have a pillar at their long end to support the strings, while open harps, such as arch harps and bow harps, do not.

features.claim: A harp's frame has a pillar at its long end that holds up the strings.
features.quote: All harps have a neck, resonator, and strings, frame harps or triangular harps have a pillar at their long end to support the strings, while open harps, such as arch harps and bow harps, do not.

features.claim: The top of each string is fixed to the crossbar or neck, where there is a tuning peg.
features.quote: The top end of each string is secured on the crossbar or neck, where each will have a tuning peg or similar device to adjust the pitch.

features.claim: Each string runs down from the crossbar to the sounding board on the resonating body, where it is tied with a knot.
features.quote: From the crossbar, the string runs down to the sounding board on the resonating body, where it is secured with a knot; on modern harps the string's hole is protected with an eyelet to limit wear on the wood.

features.claim: The strings are made of gut or wire, and often nylon or metal today.
features.quote: Strings are made of gut or wire, often replaced in the modern day by nylon or metal.

features.claim: The frame is usually a triangle made of wood.
features.quote: Harps have strings that are tied to the frame, which is usually a triangle made of wood.

features.claim: The side of the triangle that leans on the player's body is called the sound box.
features.quote: The side of the triangle that leans on the player's body is called the "sound box".

features.claim: The top side of the triangle has many pegs, one for each string.
features.quote: The top side of the triangle has a lot of pegs in it. There is one peg for each string on the harp.

second_reading.claim: The body of a harp is hollow.
second_reading.quote: The body is hollow, and when a taut string is plucked, the body resonates, projecting sound.
